title: Governance acceptance semantics: lifecycle-aware accept() + real guards for governance-shaped tasks
objective: Fix two control-plane defects this closeout exposed, both in tools/ only. (a) LIFECYCLE-AWARE ACCEPTANCE: requirement rows whose sole unmet obligations are acceptance-ordering lifecycle acts - accept itself, post-accept cleanup, checkpoint creation, and the stop-after-accept condition - must not gate accept(). They are EVALUATED, never deleted or waived, and are verified at the first post-accept opportunity instead. Today they are structurally unsatisfiable before acceptance yet required for it, which deadlocks every governance closeout. (b) CLOSE THE VACUOUS-GUARD GAP: for governance-shaped tasks whose allowed_paths lie entirely under the excluded project-control/ tree, the frozen content manifest is the deterministic empty-set hash, so accept()'s staleness check and the require_clean dirt check both compare a constant against itself and detect nothing; additionally _v2_task_unresolved never compares reviewed_sha at all. Give those tasks real staleness and dirt guards and an actual reviewed_sha comparison. No requirement row's applicability is edited in place: the append-only invariant is not holed (D-004-R627).
business_reason: Owner directive Message F item 2 (D-004-R627..R633), chosen over widening the Option-B fallback precisely because a per-task workaround would recur on every future governance closeout. The fifth independent verification pass proved the gap concretely: between f08769e1 and 16ae4589 a file inside M0-T027's allowed_paths genuinely changed and the recorded identity did not move. Eight requirement rows are currently circular with acceptance; the classification of each belongs to the independent verifier, not the producer.

acceptance_scenarios: AS-1 (executable): a governance task whose ONLY unmet applicable rows are acceptance-ordering lifecycle acts can be accepted; the rows are recorded as EVALUATED with an explicit lifecycle classification, never deleted, waived, or silently passed.
AS-2 (executable, negative): a task with ANY unmet non-lifecycle row still fails accept() exactly as today. Prove with the current M0-T027 shape that a substantive unmet row blocks acceptance.
AS-3 (executable, negative): lifecycle classification is derived from row semantics, NOT from a task-id allowlist, a bypass flag, or an environment override. Prove no special-casing exists.
AS-4 (executable): rows classified as lifecycle acts are verified at the FIRST post-accept opportunity - the mechanism exists, is reachable, and is proven by test, not merely asserted.

AS-5 (executable): for a governance-shaped task (allowed_paths entirely under project-control/), a modification to a file inside allowed_paths now MOVES the recorded staleness identity. Regression-prove the concrete case the fifth pass found: the M0-T027 packet changed between f08769e1 and 16ae4589 while the identity did not. || OWNER RULING C2 (2026-07-31, binding - cite this rather than re-litigating): the LITERAL clause of AS-5 is recorded as NOT MET and PROVEN UNMEETABLE - the CLI stamps the identity in submit() and THEN writes status/progress_percent and saves the packet, so a raw-blob control-plane identity is stale the instant it is recorded; the producer demonstrated this executably and both independent gates reproduced it. The substituted material/lifecycle reading is ACCEPTED as satisfying AS-5 IN SUBSTANCE, AS A MECHANISM. The ruling endorses the APPROACH - field-scoped identity rather than raw blob - and explicitly does NOT endorse the current 43-field exclusion list, whose boundary owner decision C1 orders tightened under a separate follow-up task.
AS-6 (executable): for the same task shape, a dirty or untracked file under project-control/ is now DETECTED by the dirt guard, which today drops it via the shared exclusion tuple.
AS-7 (executable): reviewed_sha is ACTUALLY compared in the verification layer; a stale reviewed_sha fails closed. Today _v2_task_unresolved never compares it.

AS-8 (executable, no-regression): every existing behavior is preserved - the full project-control and directive-compliance suites pass, stored history is never retro-rejected, and no previously-refused acceptance now succeeds for any non-lifecycle reason.
AS-9 (executable, containment): git diff --name-only touches only allowed_paths; no requirement row's applicability is edited; project-control/directives/** is unmodified.

AS-10 (independent, NOT the producer's call): the independent verifier classifies EACH of the eight candidate rows (D-004-R322, R323, R388, R389, R486, R487, R488, R501) as acceptance-ordering-lifecycle or not, per row, with reasons. The producer must NOT pre-classify them.

AS-11 (fact-check, recorded either way): determine whether option (iii) - re-scoping only the five rows scoped solely to M0-T027 - would ALONE have reached acceptance, given R322/R323/R389 carry additional task bindings. Record the answer and its derivation regardless of which way it comes out.

AS-12 (rider 2): the classifier's definition of 'acceptance-ordering lifecycle act' is DOCUMENTED IN THE CODE ITSELF - a docstring or spec comment stating the rule, derived from row semantics per AS-3 - so a future reviewer audits a STATED RULE rather than inferring it from behavior. An undocumented classifier fails this scenario even if its behavior is correct.

AS-13 (rider 3): the independent verifier's per-row classification of the eight (AS-10) is PRESERVED AS A TRACKED REPORT with per-row rationale, so future closeouts reuse the reasoning instead of re-deriving it and M0-T033-shaped rows inherit a precedent on paper. Written by the orchestrator from the verifier's return, verbatim; reviewers remain read-only.

AS-14 (rider 4): anything AS-5/AS-6 surface as PRE-EXISTING dirt or staleness in this repository is a DISCLOSED FINDING ONLY - reported in the producer report, and NEVER fixed, worked around, or suppressed inside this task's scope. Silently curing such a finding fails this scenario.
risks: This code decides what gets accepted. A permissive bug here silently lowers the acceptance bar for every future task, so no shortcut is acceptable because it is 'just' a control-plane fix.
Lifecycle-awareness must not become a general escape hatch: if the classifier is too broad, substantive obligations get reclassified as lifecycle and stop gating.

Tightening the staleness/dirt guards may surface pre-existing dirt in the working tree and block acceptances that previously passed; that is correct behavior but must be disclosed rather than worked around.
The producer must not classify the eight rows - that is the independent verifier's call under AS-10 and D-004-R632.

Rider 1 (owner emphasis): a lifecycle classifier one notch too permissive is the WORST outcome this task can produce - it silently lowers the acceptance bar for every future task. A rejected classifier design is a CHEAPER failure than a permissive one that passes. G3 and G5 are instructed to bear down hardest on AS-2 and AS-3.
